concepts.def: Heat transfer through solids by particle vibration and free-electron movement (in metals).
Heat transfer in fluids by warm, less-dense regions rising and cool, denser regions sinking.
Heat transfer by infrared electromagnetic waves; needs no medium.
Perfect emitter and absorber; intensity and peak wavelength depend on temperature.
Measure of how easily heat passes through a material; lower U-value means better insulation.
Loft insulation (traps air), double glazing (gas gap), cavity walls — all reduce conduction/convection.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Thermal Physics — a core area of GCSE Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Thermal Physics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Thermal Physics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
